title: Incremental JSONL Protocol and SDK Adaptor Playground
body:
Purpose and brief
This is a working PRD / playground doc exploring an incremental, newline-delimited JSON (JSONL) framing for partial structured output that balances low-latency streaming, deterministic tooling handoffs, and simple client-side parsing. Target: hosted API streaming responses that may emit partially-complete structured objects, tool-call frames, and resumable checkpoints that SDKs can cheaply materialize and reconcile.

Why this direction?
- Many SDKs (mobile JS/Python/Go) want a very small surface to parse: streaming text tokens are messy; JSONL lines are easier to incrementally decode and validate.
- Typed tool-calls (function-like frames) benefit from discrete frames with deterministic boundaries to avoid partial-JSON problems.
- Lightweight resumability: newline boundaries give us safe checkpoints where a client can request a resume token and the service can replay from last committed line.

High-level protocol sketch (incremental JSONL)
- Each server-sent line is a single JSON object followed by \n. Types: 'meta', 'chunk', 'tool_call', 'commit', 'error'.
- 'chunk' contains {id, seq, partial_payload: string | null, schema_version}. The client appends partial_payload onto a buffer for the id.
- 'tool_call' contains {id, tool_name, args: object, call_id} and is treated as an atomic action: SDKs should emit a typed hook and stop merging into the text buffer.
- 'commit' contains {id, seq, checksum, resume_cursor}. When commit emitted, server considers that logical object stable; clients may persist resume_cursor.
- 'meta' contains session-level signals: {model, variant, latency_hint, experimental_flags}.
- 'error' contains structured error code + optional recoverability hint.

Operational semantics and guarantees (best-effort)
- Ordering: lines are strictly ordered; sequence numbers enable client-side detection of missing lines.
- Idempotency: resume_cursor is opaque token; replay from cursor must move forward deterministically for a few seconds (bounded).
- Backpressure: clients can send a resume / throttle signal on the control channel; server respects best-effort politeness.
- Size constraints: single JSONL line must be <= 64KB to keep parsing cheap; chunked payloads are allowed (seq increments) for larger outputs.

SDK adaptor patterns (developer ergonomics)
- Minimal contract: SDK exposes an iterator/async generator that yields either "partial_update", "tool_request", or "final_commit" events. The onus of token merging lives in the SDK, not the user.
- JS SDK behavior (browser): incremental TextDecoder + newline scanning -> parse each complete line into JSON -> dispatch typed event. Provide small helper: assemblePartial(id) -> returns current buffered string + progress percent.
- Python SDK behavior: similar generator interface; add optional validate(schema) call to run jsonschema checks on each commit.
- Mobile/Embedded: provide a tiny C shim that scans bytes for \n and emits protobuf-friendly typed events for downstream apps. Keep memory bounded by per-id sliding window.

Tool-calling ergonomics
- tool_call frames are atomic and must include a call_id. The SDK should expose a tool registry where app code registers call handlers. When a tool_call appears, the SDK pauses regular text delivery for that id until the tool returns a resolution (sync or async).
- Default: if the app does not register the tool handler, SDK emits a 'tool_unhandled' event; server may then fall back to an internal tool resolution strategy or return an error frame.
- Security: tool_call frames must carry a capability boolean (can_invoke_tool) bound to the API key scope. Servers must reject tool_call frames that require elevated capabilities if not present.

Structured output migration path
- Phase 0 (experiments): produce JSONL only for developer feature flags and non-critical flows. SDKs include opt-in flag streaming= "jsonl_experiment_v1".
- Phase 1 (beta): enable commit frames for final objects and provide full jsonschema in meta frames so SDKs can validate.
- Phase 2 (GA): switch default streaming protocol for structured outputs to JSONL with backward-compatible text proxy for plain-text clients for 6 months.

Observability and debugging hooks
- Emit telemetry: per-line latency, parse_error_count, tool_call_latency, resume_replay_rate.
- Add a debug mode where servers include a special 'annot' meta line that maps line seq -> internal token offsets to help triage fuzz mis-parses.
- Provide a small CLI tool (playground) that can ingest a JSONL stream and visualize per-id buffers and tool call lifecycle. (prototype in linked PR)

Performance & cost considerations
- JSONL framing adds ~2–5% bytes overhead vs raw tokens but enables clients to compress and de-duplicate commits, likely reducing downstream compute by allowing caching at object-level.
- Ensure that chunk size and commit frequency are knobs: aggressive commits increase throughput to backend storage and observability events (cost), but reduce rework on retries.

Security and privacy notes
- Resume cursors are ephemeral and opaque; do not leak PII. Limit replay window (e.g., 30s–2min depending on model workload).
- Tool calls must be authorized. Consider per-route capability flags and audit logs tied to call_id.

Open questions / tradeoffs (notes to self)
- How to handle very large single JSON objects: stream inside the JSON value vs chunking the object across sequences? Chunking is simpler but increases complexity for checksum/validation.
- Resumability semantics across model rollbacks: if model variant changes between resume and replay, should server map cursor -> nearest compatible variant or force client to restart?
- Schema evolution: embed schema_version in meta frames but need a migration strategy for old SDKs. Consider inline schema diffs rather than full copies for commits.
- Tool-call timeouts: if a client receives tool_call and does not respond, should server continue generation or fallback? For low-latency UX, we need a default server-side fallback policy.

Prototype TODOs (practical next steps)
- [ ] Finalize line envelope spec (fields, max sizes). Owner: Daniel. Linear: PROD-482.
- [ ] Implement JS SDK incremental parser and expose async generator with event types. Owner: Marcel. PR: #673.
- [ ] Build small CLI visualizer (python) that reads a saved JSONL session and shows per-id buffer progression. Owner: Priya.
- [ ] Wire telemetry events in staging and add dashboards for parse_error_count and resume_replay_rate. Owner: Observability.
- [ ] Run a canary: enable JSONL for 5% of low-latency hosts and measure error delta + bytes delta. Owner: product-hosted-api.

Appendix: small example stream (human readable)
meta {
  "type": "meta",
  "model": "rw-medium-v2",
  "schema_version": "2025-11-01"
}
chunk {
  "type": "chunk",
  "id": "resp-42",
  "seq": 1,
  "partial_payload": "{\"title\": \"Draft API doc\""
}
chunk {
  "type": "chunk",
  "id": "resp-42",
  "seq": 2,
  "partial_payload": " , \"sections\": [\"intro\" ] }"
}
tool_call {
  "type": "tool_call",
  "id": "resp-42",
  "tool_name": "lookup-knowledge",
  "args": {"query": "redwood shortcode spec"},
  "call_id": "tc-1"
}
commit {
  "type": "commit",
  "id": "resp-42",
  "seq": 3,
  "checksum": "sha256:abcd...",
  "resume_cursor": "curs:eyJzZXNzaW9uIjoxMjM0fQ=="
}

(above is illustrative; actual frames are single-line JSON objects separated by newlines)

Quick rationale summary (for exec audience)
- Small protocol change yields better SDK ergonomics, simpler tool-call handoff, and clear resumability semantics. It trades a little wire overhead for huge developer productivity gains when building deterministic tool integrations and structured-output apps.

Notes: this is intentionally a rough working doc — expectations: lots of follow-ups, experiments first, then a careful migration plan.
